messages.content:
You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: According to the GitLab Ireland Ltd Right to Disconnect Policy, what should be included in every meeting invitation?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): Every meeting invite should link an agenda.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Ireland Ltd Right to Disconnect Policy > Roles and Responsibilities > 9. Meetings]
The Company asks that we be respectful of others' time and consider the time investment others are asked to make when attending meetings. Try to avoid meetings, and if one is necessary, try to make attendance optional for as many people as possible. All meetings should have an agenda linked from the invite, and you should document the outcome. Instead of having people ask permission, trust their judgement and offer a consultation process if they have questions.

[GitLab Ireland Ltd Right to Disconnect Policy > Roles and Responsibilities > 11. Raising concerns]
The effectiveness of the Policy will be reviewed as required and we encourage team members to speak with their manager or a member of Team Member Relations if they have any concerns regarding this Policy including potential violation by others. If a team member believes that their manager is not complying with the Policy, or otherwise is not comfortable raising an issue regarding the Policy with their manager, the team member may contact Team Member Relations at teammemberrelations@gitlab.com. Team members who do not comply with this Policy may be subject to disciplinary action.

[GitLab Ireland Ltd Right to Disconnect Policy > Roles and Responsibilities > 5. Commitment and responsibilities]
The Company commits to monitoring and enforcing this Policy. With this in mind, the Company believes that it is important to set out expectations for both managers and individual contributors.

(a) Managers

It is the responsibility of all managers to:

(i) know the regular working hours of their direct reports, and communicate any changes in scheduling to team members in as timely a manner as possible;
(ii) set clear and reasonable expectations with respect to workload and  deliverables;
(iii) set clear and reasonable expectations with respect to when work, and engaging in work-related communications, outside of regular working hours may be required as a normal part of the team member's job;
(iv) ensure that team members are taking statutory breaks, vacation, and other rest periods as may be required by law;
(v) ensure that other team members are complying with the Policy when communicating with their co-workers;
(vi) not penalise or unfairly treat a team member for exercising their rights under this Policy or any relevant legislation; and

(b) Individual Contributors
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
According to the policy, all meetings should have an agenda linked from the invite [1].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
